extracted.intended_audience: patent attorneys, judges, and advanced law students
extracted.subtask_description: Authoritative, practice-oriented standards and doctrinal rules governing patentability, specification and claim requirements, prosecution and litigation topics (e.g., disclosure, drawings, disclaimers, estoppel, diligence, equivalents, equity remedies). Targeted at legal practitioners adjudicating or preparing patents/suits.

rubrics_metrics.name: Deceit in procuring assignment
rubrics_metrics.description: DECEIT IN PROCURING ASSIGNMENT, what is, proof of; remedy of assignee for deceit; assignments rescinded when.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Discusses what constitutes deceit in obtaining an assignment, evidentiary proof required, remedies available to an assignee, and circumstances when assignments are rescinded. Cross-references: Assignee, Assignment, Assignor, Equity, Rescission, Warranty.

rubrics_metrics.name: Decrees in equity (as estoppel)
rubrics_metrics.description: DECREES in equity — by consent as an estoppel.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A decree entered by consent may operate as an estoppel. See also Action in Equity, Collusive Suit, Injunctions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Defects in letters-patent and amendments
rubrics_metrics.description: DEFECTS — mode of removing from existing arts is a new art; defects in letters-patent not curable by strained interpretation; amendment provisions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Addresses which defects in a patent or specification can be cured by amendment or interpretation and which are incurable; cross-references include Ambiguity, Amendment, Claim, Construction, Description, Errors, Letters-Patent, Re-issues, Substance and Form.

rubrics_metrics.name: Defences in patent litigation
rubrics_metrics.description: DEFENCES — defenses to infringement suits (at law or in equity); favored in equity; defenses to assignor's action for purchase money and to licensor's action for royalties.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explains available defenses in actions at law and in equity, how equity treats certain defenses more favorably, and specific defenses in assignor/licensor contexts. Cross-references: Action in Equity, Action at Law, Assignment, Deceit, Estoppel, Laches, License, Royalties.

rubrics_metrics.name: Treatment of defendant in patent suits
rubrics_metrics.description: DEFENDANT — submitting to jurisdiction waives defects; defendant's patent admissible; prima facie evidence of novelty and utility; disclaimers may estop defendant; various estoppel and procedural rules.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Points include: waiver by submission to jurisdiction; patents of defendant admissible; a defendant's patent may be prima facie evidence of novelty/utility but validity may not be in issue; disclaimers can estop the defendant; suppression/concealment may be prejudicial. Also covers joinder/nonjoinder, inspection of books, and equitable examination of profits. See related headings (Admissions, Burden of Proof, Estoppel, Infringement, Injunction).

rubrics_metrics.name: Effect of delay in applying for patent
rubrics_metrics.description: DELAY — effect of delay in applying for patent; not ipso facto abandonment to public; may estop first inventor from claiming as against later rival; 'unavoidable' and 'unreasonable' defined; effect in re-issue and suits (laches).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specifies that delay is not automatically abandonment, but may have consequences (estoppel, impact on prior inventor's rights); after-application delay not abandonment if unavoidable; Patent Office delay can't prejudice inventor; unreasonable delay may show abandonment in re-issue; connection to laches in suits. Cross-references: Abandonment, Application for Patent, Diligence, Re-issues, Rival Inventors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Depositions in equity
rubrics_metrics.description: DEPOSITIONS IN EQUITY — how taken; objections to evidence when referred to court.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Covers procedural rules for taking depositions in equity cases, timing of objections, and interplay with court references. See Actions in Equity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Requirement to describe the invention
rubrics_metrics.description: DESCRIBE — if the applicant cannot describe he cannot have invented.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Fundamental proposition that description is essential to claiming invention; inability to describe undermines claim to invention.

rubrics_metrics.name: Describing without claiming leads to abandonment
rubrics_metrics.description: DESCRIBING AND NOT CLAIMING — when describing and not claiming, may constitute abandonment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Describing an invention in the specification but failing to claim it can lead to abandonment (but not necessarily ipso facto abandonment in all circumstances); relates to re-issues and public abandonment doctrines.

rubrics_metrics.name: Description and claim both essential
rubrics_metrics.description: DESCRIPTION AND CLAIM — both essential to patent; distinct; how written; must correspond; claim controls; contradictory matter may void both; claim cannot be enlarged by description.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Detailed requirements and rules: the specification and the claims are both essential and distinct; they must correspond and be consistent; a claim controls construction; contradictory description and claim may be void; description cannot be used to enlarge the claim. Cross-references: Ambiguity, Application for Patent, Claim, Drawings, Re-issues, Specification.

rubrics_metrics.name: Specification sufficiency and disclosure requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: DESCRIPTION — must set forth a new invention in fact; must fully disclose attributes; explain mode of making and practical use; must render the invention accessible to the public; must show best mode of making and of using; may omit well-known parts; concealing anything to advantage of inventor makes patent void.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specification must be correct, complete, and intelligible; may be sufficient if intelligible to those skilled in the art; defects immaterial if skilled persons could remedy them; insufficient if workmen must try further experiments; illustrated by drawings and model; false suggestions are fatal; completeness defined; sufficiency is a question for jury and judged by skilled artisans. Also addresses chemical processes, omission of scientific principle, and how a description of result is inadequate as description of means.

rubrics_metrics.name: Form and tone of specification
rubrics_metrics.description: DESCRIPTION (form): not to be argumentative; ordinary meaning of words governed by general statements; how old and new are distinguished; examples of form issues.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specification should avoid eulogizing or disparaging; ordinary meanings depend on general statements within spec; must separate new from old; form-of-description considerations (examples, genus/species guidance), and that specification is not evidence of prior use.

rubrics_metrics.name: Design patent requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: DESIGN — definition and requirements: must affect physical substance; resides in appearance, not utility; consists in form (configuration/ornamentation), not color or material; must be new; essence tested by impression on the mind through the eye.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Design is the appearance imparted to a substance; may be patentable even if not more beautiful; can coexist with a manufacture; distinct from device producing it; drawings and description requirements; joinder and claims for designs; infringement and profits rules for designs. Cross-references: Appearance, Claim, Drawings, Identity, Reduction to Practice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rights of devisee/representative of deceased inventor
rubrics_metrics.description: DEVisee / EXECUTOR / DECEASED INVENTOR — rights of devisee or executor to patents; remedy on death of plaintiff pending suit; who may apply for patents after death.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rules on vesting and prosecution of patents after inventor's death, who may sue, how title vests, and duties of executor/representative (including applying for or extending patents). Cross-references: Deceased Inventor, Title issues.

rubrics_metrics.name: Diligence in reduction to practice
rubrics_metrics.description: DILIGENCE — in reducing to practice; not required of sole inventor; necessary to first conceiver but not to later conceiver; 'reasonable diligence' is required; connects conception and reduction as one continuous inventive act; measure of diligence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Early conceiver must show diligence from date of conception to reduction; no 'race of diligence'; reasonable diligence is the standard; lack of diligence may estop a prior inventor from claiming when later rival reduces to practice. Cross-references: Date of Conception, Reduction to Practice, Rival Inventors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Disclaimer as method of amending/correcting patents
rubrics_metrics.description: DISCLAIMER — object and character; a mode of amending a defective patent; distinction between disclaimer and re-issue; may cure excessive claims; may relinquish claimed method; cannot enlarge scope; must be filed without unreasonable delay; estoppel effects.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Twofold purpose: to amend defective patents and to save otherwise lost suits. Statutory/regulatory constraints exist; disclaimer amends only excessive claims and cannot correct certain substantive mistakes; must be timely and without fraud; effects limited territorially and to interests of disclaimant; becomes part of original specification and leaves patent as if originally issued in amended form; may estop parties. Cross-references: Amendment, Re-issues, Claims, Estoppel, Patent Office practice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Disclosure as consideration for grant
rubrics_metrics.description: DISCLOSURE — disclosure of the invention in the patent is the consideration of the grant.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The act of disclosure in the specification is the quid pro quo for the monopoly; insufficent disclosure undermines the grant. See also Specification requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Discovery as part of inventive act
rubrics_metrics.description: DISCOVERIES — discovery essential to inventive act; relates to force, object, or mode of application; seven forms of discovery; must be evidenced and reduction to practice completed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Discovery alone without construction and reduction is not invention; evidence of discovery may include intrinsic novelty or prior unsuccessful efforts; discovery is an element evaluated in pleadings and equity remedies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Doctrine of double use
rubrics_metrics.description: DOUBLE USE — doctrine concerning new uses of old things and whether new use constitutes invention; assumes identity of invention used; may or may not be an improvement; applies to designs; new use of force or object distinctions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Discusses when a new use of a patented article or force applied to a new object constitutes patentable invention; divisions between specific treatment of specific objects, combinations, and out-of-combination uses; historical misconceptions and practical applications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Drawings for Patent Office
rubrics_metrics.description: DRAWINGS — when required; necessity/sufficiency determined by Commissioner; must correspond with specification; cannot supply place of written description; must be clear and full to supply place of model; must show every feature claimed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Drawings may show invention where specification fails but cannot replace a written description; imperfect drawings can create fatal ambiguity; need not be working drawings; signature and requisites vary by class of invention; drawings generally cannot be amended in the Office; may be withdrawn after filing; not evidence of reduction to practice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Elements of combination — identity and claim effect
rubrics_metrics.description: ELEMENTS OF COMBINATION — defined; distinct from the combination as inventions; an unnecessary part is not an element unless so claimed; elements described and claimed make them essential.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Elements of a combination are distinct units; once claimed they become essential whether actually essential or not; unclaimed elements are conceded old; joinder with claims for combinations and subcombinations; re-issue considerations; use of less than all elements may not be infringement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Embodiments belong to inventor
rubrics_metrics.description: EMBODIMENT — all forms of embodiment belong to the inventor.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: All forms and variations of an invention that are disclosed or derived from the inventive concept are part of the inventor's rights; relation to reduction to practice and claim coverage.

rubrics_metrics.name: Employee/employer rights and contracts
rubrics_metrics.description: EMPLOYEE / EMPLOYER — employee relation to employer bearing on rights to inventions; assignment to employer and how shown; no employer right except under contract/assignment/license.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Patenting rights between employer and employee depend on contract terms, assignment, or other agreements; ancillary inventions may belong to employer in some circumstances; corporate employer liability for infringing acts; cross references to assignment, contracts, and estoppel.

rubrics_metrics.name: End or effect is not an invention
rubrics_metrics.description: END OR EFFECT — defined; not an invention; distinguished from function; proposed end is satisfaction of a want; idea often accomplished by different means.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Patent law treats an intended end or effect as insufficient for patentability; invention must be in the means or apparatus producing the result rather than the abstract end. Comparative utility or improved convenience alone does not demonstrate inventive means.

rubrics_metrics.name: Equity jurisdiction and remedies in patent cases
rubrics_metrics.description: EQUITY / EQUITY JURISDICTION — general rules; equity still distinct from law; will compel conveyance to true owner; relief available where legal remedy is inadequate; local differences; when injunctions/discovery appropriate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explains when equitable relief (injunctions, accountings, rescission) lies in patent disputes: adequacy of legal remedies, the need for discovery, timing relative to patent expiration, local enforcement issues, and limits where only damages or contractual relief exist. Cross-references: Injunction, Damages, Licensee rights.

rubrics_metrics.name: Doctrine of equivalents
rubrics_metrics.description: EQUIVALENTS — doctrine of equivalents: must be capable of substitution, perform same functions, be known to perform those functions at patent date, not change result; resides in use and effect, not nature.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Equivalents may be entirely unlike in name/character but still infringe if they perform same function in same way to achieve same result; governed by special rules for chemical vs mechanical inventions; question of fact for jury; equivalents covered by claims and may support infringement findings even if not literally claimed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Estoppel doctrines in patent law
rubrics_metrics.description: ESTOPPEL — at law and in equity; acts and representations can estop parties (disclaimers, admissions, permits, silence, neglect); favored as a defense in equity; estoppel applies to assignors, licensees, and others.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Estoppel may prevent a party from asserting defenses or denying facts (utility, ownership, identity) based on prior conduct, disclaimers, admissions, or failure to sue. Patent Office and court estoppel doctrines differ; estoppel may be limited by contract scope and territorial interests.

rubrics_metrics.name: Evidence rules in patent proceedings
rubrics_metrics.description: EVIDENCE — direct and circumstantial comparative value; negative evidence importance; Patent Office evidence rules same as courts; evidence in interferences and in equity; order of introduction in actions at law.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Addresses admissibility and weight of different types of evidence, differences between equity and law regarding evidence, timing for objections, suppression motions, and special rules in Patent Office and interference proceedings. See related headings for procedural detail.

rubrics_metrics.name: Duties and limits of Patent Office examiners
rubrics_metrics.description: EXAMINERS in Patent Office — duties of examiners; status as agents or judicial officers; must follow Commissioner's decisions and rules; interviews with applicants; jurisdictional limits in certain issues.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examiners' scope: they are bound by precedent and Commissioner's rulings, handle interviews, may have limited jurisdiction over patentability in some proceedings, and have exclusive jurisdiction in declared interferences. Their role changed historically (agents to judicial officers).

rubrics_metrics.name: Examination of patent applications
rubrics_metrics.description: EXAMINATION — examination of applications in the Patent Office; procedures and standards (see Application for Patent).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: References the general statutory and procedural framework for examination, including use of rules, evidence, and the Commissioner's authority; cross-references to Application for Patent and Examination headings.
